scenes.visual: Title card 'Sliding, Not Shrinking' over a flexing arm silhouette whose biceps is drawn as a bundle of thin red fibres. COLOUR MAP (used in both films): actin thin filament BLUE, myosin thick filament and heads ORANGE, calcium YELLOW dots, tropomyosin DARK GREY strand, troponin small PURPLE block, ATP GREEN dots, Z disc BLACK vertical bar, store (sarcoplasmic reticulum) PALE TEAL sleeve. Proteins are labelled blocks and rods, never molecular structures.

scenes.tts: A muscle fibre shortens, yet none of its filaments gets any shorter. How can that be? Let's zoom in and watch one contract.
scenes.visual: Camera dives from the arm into one long red fibre, then into a striped strand inside it. A question card: 'The fibre shortens. Do its filaments?' The stripes pulse gently.
scenes.narration: A muscle fibre shortens, yet none of its filaments gets any shorter. How can that be? Let's zoom in and watch one contract.

scenes.tts: A skeletal muscle fibre is one long cell. It is packed with chains of repeating units called sarcomeres. Each sarcomere runs from one Z disc to the next.
scenes.visual: The strand resolves into a row of identical boxes; one box is highlighted and labelled 'sarcomere', with BLACK bars at each end labelled 'Z disc'. A bracket spans Z disc to Z disc.
scenes.narration: A skeletal muscle fibre is one long cell. It is packed with chains of repeating units called sarcomeres. Each sarcomere runs from one Z disc to the next.

scenes.tts: Thin filaments of actin hang from each Z disc. A thick filament of myosin sits in the middle. Its heads stick out toward the actin on both sides.
scenes.visual: Inside the highlighted sarcomere, BLUE rods grow inward from both BLACK Z discs, labelled 'actin (thin)'. A thick ORANGE rod appears in the middle, labelled 'myosin (thick)', with small ORANGE heads. Heads on the left half point left, heads on the right half point right; small arrows show this.
scenes.narration: Thin filaments of actin hang from each Z disc. A thick filament of myosin sits in the middle. Its heads stick out toward the actin on both sides.

scenes.tts: At rest, a strand called tropomyosin covers the sites where myosin binds. Calcium is the switch. In skeletal and heart muscle, it binds troponin, and troponin moves tropomyosin aside.
scenes.visual: A DARK GREY strand lies along each BLUE rod over small white notches labelled 'myosin-binding sites'. A nerve symbol flashes at the edge; YELLOW dots spill from the PALE TEAL sleeve around the sarcomere. Dots land on PURPLE troponin blocks, and the DARK GREY strand rolls off the notches. Corner label 'skeletal and heart muscle'.
scenes.narration: At rest, a strand called tropomyosin covers the sites where myosin binds. Calcium is the switch. In skeletal and heart muscle, it binds troponin, and troponin moves tropomyosin aside.

scenes.tts: Now the myosin heads grab actin and swing. Heads on each half pull toward the middle. So both sets of thin filaments slide inward.
scenes.visual: ORANGE heads latch onto the BLUE notches and tilt toward the centre. Both BLUE rod sets slide inward together; motion arrows on each side point to the middle.
scenes.narration: Now the myosin heads grab actin and swing. Heads on each half pull toward the middle. So both sets of thin filaments slide inward.

scenes.tts: The Z discs draw together, and the sarcomere shortens. But the thick filament keeps its length, and so do the thin ones. Only their overlap changes.
scenes.visual: BLACK Z discs move inward. A ruler bar over the ORANGE rod stays the same length, labelled 'thick filament: same length'; a ruler over one BLUE rod also stays fixed. A shaded band where BLUE and ORANGE overlap widens, labelled 'overlap grows'. A side-by-side 'before / after' freeze holds for a second.
scenes.narration: The Z discs draw together, and the sarcomere shortens. But the thick filament keeps its length, and so do the thin ones. Only their overlap changes.

scenes.tts: Each head pulls only a tiny distance. Then it must let go and grab again further along. ATP binds, and the head lets go. ATP is split, and the head re-cocks. Then it grabs actin again and swings once more.
scenes.visual: Close-up on one ORANGE head on a BLUE rod. A GREEN dot docks on the head: the head lifts off, label 'ATP binds: let go'. The GREEN dot splits into two smaller GREEN pieces and the head tilts back, label 'ATP split: re-cock'. The head lands one notch further along, swings, and the pieces drift away, label 'swing = the pull'. The cycle loops twice, quicker the second time.
scenes.narration: Each head pulls only a tiny distance. Then it must let go and grab again further along. ATP binds, and the head lets go. ATP is split, and the head re-cocks. Then it grabs actin again and swings once more.

scenes.tts: Here is a question for you. Take away all the ATP. Do the heads stay stuck to actin, or do they fall off?
scenes.visual: All GREEN dots fade out of the scene. Heads are frozen mid-cycle, some attached. Question card: 'No ATP: stuck or free?'
scenes.narration: Here is a question for you. Take away all the ATP. Do the heads stay stuck to actin, or do they fall off?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: They stay stuck. Without ATP, an attached head cannot let go, so the fibre locks stiff. That is why muscles stiffen after death, the state called rigor mortis.
scenes.visual: Most attached ORANGE heads stay clamped onto BLUE (some heads were never attached and stay free); a lock icon appears on the sarcomere. Pull back to a cartoon arm outline turning rigid, label 'rigor mortis: heads cannot let go'.
scenes.narration: They stay stuck. Without ATP, an attached head cannot let go, so the fibre locks stiff. That is why muscles stiffen after death, the state called rigor mortis.

scenes.tts: One sarcomere moves only a hair. So how does that become a pull you can see? The answer is in how sarcomeres are arranged.
scenes.visual: Back to one shortening sarcomere, tiny on screen, label 'one sarcomere: a tiny shift'. The camera begins to pull back.
scenes.narration: One sarcomere moves only a hair. So how does that become a pull you can see? The answer is in how sarcomeres are arranged.

scenes.tts: A long fibre holds tens of thousands of sarcomeres in a row. Each one shortens a little. Their small shortenings add up along the chain into one visible pull.
scenes.visual: Pull back: the sarcomere becomes one link in a long chain of identical sarcomeres. All shorten together; small arrows at each Z disc. A marker at the chain's end slides a visible distance, label 'chain end moves the sum'. On-screen note: 'schematic: real fibres hold tens of thousands in a row'.
scenes.narration: A long fibre holds tens of thousands of sarcomeres in a row. Each one shortens a little. Their small shortenings add up along the chain into one visible pull.

scenes.tts: Notice what this machine can do. It can pull its ends together. It cannot push them apart.
scenes.visual: The chain shortens; then an arrow tries to push it longer and a red X appears over the arrow. Label 'muscles only pull'.
scenes.narration: Notice what this machine can do. It can pull its ends together. It cannot push them apart.

scenes.tts: So every muscle needs something to stretch it back. In your arm, one muscle bends the elbow and another straightens it. Each takes a turn pulling.
scenes.visual: Cartoon upper arm with two muscles drawn as red bands: front band shortens and the forearm bends; then the back band shortens and the forearm straightens, stretching the front band. Labels 'bends', 'straightens'.
scenes.narration: So every muscle needs something to stretch it back. In your arm, one muscle bends the elbow and another straightens it. Each takes a turn pulling.

scenes.tts: Filaments slide; they never shrink. Many small slides in a row add up to one pull. Every muscle in this lesson pulls with this same machine. They differ in how calcium throws the switch.
scenes.visual: Recap strip: sarcomere sliding (BLUE and ORANGE), chain of sarcomeres, arm pair. Below, three small icons with YELLOW switch symbols: a heart, a gut tube, a fly, with a question mark over each switch, label 'same machine, different switches'.
scenes.narration: Filaments slide; they never shrink. Many small slides in a row add up to one pull. Every muscle in this lesson pulls with this same machine. They differ in how calcium throws the switch.

scenes.visual: End card with the mascot and one line only: 'Filaments slide, never shrink; many small slides add up to one pull.'
